Hi Fernando, this is Marcos from IT. I want to explain what happened last night. At about seven ten, my team was updating the scheduling system. While we were installing the update, the main server suddenly crashed. We noticed the problem in two minutes, but the restart took almost an hour. Meanwhile, the doctors were using paper forms, so the patients were safe, and no data was lost. I know you were presenting to the partners in Boston, and I am really sorry about the interruption. By Friday, we will have a second server ready. If it happens again, the system will move to the second server in seconds. Call me if you have any questions.

Let me tell you about my worst presentation. It was five years ago, at a big conference in Chicago. I was speaking to about three hundred people, and everything was going well. Suddenly, the fire alarm started. Everybody stood up and walked outside. We were standing in the street for forty minutes, and it was very cold. When we came back, half of the audience was not there anymore. I felt terrible. But then a man in the first row said: Please, start again. We want to hear the end. So I started again, slowly and calmly. In the end, it was my best talk of the year. The lesson? An incident is not the end of the story. How you handle it is the story.
